items.text: At the end of the 1700s Wixárika communities received land titles that defined the boundaries of their present-day communities.

items.text: In Baja California the Kumiai call themselves Tipai. Their communities sit on the coastal plateaus of Ensenada and Rosarito and in Tecate.

items.text: Warihó and Macurawe families weave baskets, mats and hats from palm and fiber and build harps, violins and guitars. Their craft work is family based and rests with women.

items.text: In 1859 Congress set aside 372,000 acres along the Gila River as Arizona’s first reservation, in appreciation of the Akimel O’otham role in America’s westward expansion.

items.text: Hopi government is unicameral, with all powers vested in the Tribal Council. Villages choose their representatives by election or by appointment from the village leader, for two year terms.

items.text: Since 2017 the Acoma Language Program has been building the H’aakume Keres Dictionary for tribal members, with about 5,000 words and phrases being edited by fluent speakers.
